coverage_gaps: The merged universe is still US-heavy and should be expanded with Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Europe, and A-share suppliers, especially in HBM, substrates, OSAT, server ODMs, optics, and semiconductor equipment.

Layer 1B evidence for Asian memory leaders such as SK hynix and Samsung, server ODMs such as Quanta/Wiwynn/Foxconn, and optics/connector suppliers should be added before treating the universe as globally complete.
Market-pricing checks were not performed in this Layer 1C pass; valuation, consensus expectations, recent price moves, estimate revisions, short interest, and positioning must be checked separately.
Software AI monetization remains less uniform than infrastructure demand; application-layer names should be validated using incremental AI revenue, retention, pricing, and gross-margin evidence.
Power and nuclear-linked candidates require timeline discipline: near-term data-center power procurement and grid equipment are different from long-cycle nuclear or SMR deployment.
Private-company chokepoints are underrepresented, including AI model labs, private data-center developers, private optical component vendors, and hyperscaler-owned custom silicon programs.

The current candidate list prioritizes large and liquid public-market mappings; smaller component, testing, substrate, thermal, and specialty materials suppliers may contain important chokepoints but need separate validation.

memory_update.text: AI Layer 1 universe should be tracked as a multi-node infrastructure and software adoption system, not as a single accelerator-stock theme.

Top Layer 1C chokepoint candidates are accelerator silicon, advanced-node foundry, advanced packaging, HBM, AI networking, EDA, semiconductor equipment, server/rack integration, and data-center power/cooling.
HBM plus advanced packaging remains a high-priority bottleneck cluster because it combines technical difficulty, supplier concentration, qualification requirements, and capacity expansion lead times.
AI networking should remain separate from accelerators because cluster scaling can shift constraints into switch silicon, NICs, optical DSPs, lasers, transceivers, and cabling.
Data-center power and cooling should remain a core AI infrastructure node because rack density, grid interconnection, thermal constraints, and firm-power procurement can limit AI capacity deployment.
Layer 2 should add non-US suppliers across HBM, substrates, OSAT, optics, server ODMs, test equipment, thermal components, and electrical equipment.
Before candidate escalation, perform market-pricing checks to separate under-researched bottlenecks from already-consensus AI beneficiaries.

summary: Layer 1C merged the AI Layer 1A theme map and Layer 1B node-level candidates into a deduplicated initial research universe. The universe is ranked by Serenity relevance: proximity to AI demand, bottleneck likelihood, capacity or qualification constraints, direct revenue linkage, and usefulness as a public-market proxy. The highest-priority clusters are AI accelerators/custom ASICs, advanced foundry and packaging, HBM/memory, semiconductor equipment and EDA, high-speed networking/optics, AI servers/rack integration, cloud hyperscalers, and data-center power/cooling. This is a research-prioritization universe only, not a buy/sell list.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
